chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Awrama, from ‘Alī ibn Hassān, from ‘Abd al-Rahmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, regarding His, the Exalted’s, saying:
“And they were guided to the goodly word, and they were guided to the path of the Praised One.”
He عليه السلام said: “That is Hamza, and Ja‘far, and ‘Ubaydah, and Salmān, and Abū Dharr, and al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, and ‘Ammār; they were guided to Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام.”
And His saying: “He has endeared faith to you and adorned it in your hearts, and He has made hateful to you disbelief, transgression, and disobedience.”
Meaning Amīr al-Mu’minīn, and the first, and the second, and the third.

key_terms.الطَّيِّبِ: the goodly or pure, referring here to the divinely approved word
key_terms.الْإِيمَانَ: faith, interpreted here in relation to Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام
key_terms.صِرَاطِ الْحَمِيدِ: the path of the Praised One, interpreted here as guidance connected to rightful authority

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام interpret these Qur'anic verses regarding the wilayah of Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a Qur'anic commentary in which the Imam عليه السلام interprets guidance to the goodly word and the praised path as guidance to Amīr al-Mu’minīn عليه السلام. It also interprets faith as referring to him, while disbelief, transgression, and disobedience are applied to the first, second, and third.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of the Exalted
[22:24] And they are Guided to goodly words and they are Guided to the Path of the Praised One.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘That (refers to) Hamza<sup>as</sup>, and Ja’far<sup>as</sup>, and Ubeyda, and Salman<sup>as</sup>, and Abu Zarr<sup>as</sup>, and Al-Miqdad Bin Al-Aswad<sup>as</sup>, and Ammar being Guided to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>.
And Hisazwj Words [49:7] but Allah has Endeared the faith to you and has Adorned it in your hearts, and He has made hateful to you the unbelief and transgression and disobedience
– the first (Caliph), and the second (Caliph) and the third (Caliph)’.
en.sarwar: 71ـ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ يَحْيَى عَنِ ابْنِ مَحْبُوبٍ عَنْ جَمِيلِ بْنِ صَالِحٍ عَنْ أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلام) عَنْ قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى ائْتُونِي بِكِتابٍ مِنْ قَبْلِ هذا أَوْ أَثارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ قَالَ عَنَى بِالْكِتَابِ التَّوْرَاةَ وَالانْجِيلَ وَأَثَارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ فَإِنَّمَا عَنَى بِذَلِكَ عِلْمَ أَوْصِيَاءِ الانْبِيَاءِ (عَلَيْهم السَّلام). 71. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from abu ‘Ubayda who has said the following.
“I asked abu Ja‘far (a.s.) about the meaning of the words of Allah, the Most High. “. .

Bring me a Book, revealed before this Quran, or any other proof based on knowledge to support your belief, if indeed you are truthful.” [46:4]. The Imam (a.s.) said, “Book refers to Tura and the Gospel and knowledge refers to the knowledge of the executors of the wills of the prophets.”
